content.title: About
content.content: Cow head is a meat portion that includes the brain, cheeks, tongue and other organs. It is widely used in traditional cuisines around the world for soups, pâtés, roasts and charcuterie. The meat is rich in collagen and has a deep, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cow head is considered a delicacy in many Eastern European and Asian cuisines.
The brain and cheeks are high in gelatin, which creates a rich broth when simmered slowly.
Tongue is often prepared separately, marinated and grilled.
Traditional Russian "head" soup is made from the whole head with vegetables and spices.
In the United States, parts of the head are used to make head cheese and other sausages.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Head meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of collagen
items.content: Gelatinous parts supply collagen, supporting skin, joint and connective‑tissue health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, which aid blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Compared with many other cuts, head meat has a moderate amount of fat when prepared without added oils.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: The head can harbor blood residues and bacteria, so it must be thoroughly cleaned and cooked to a safe internal temperature.

items.title: High cholesterol
items.content: Certain parts, especially the brain, are high in cholesterol, so people with cardiovascular concerns should limit intake.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of gelatinous tissue can cause stomach discomfort in people with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The head can be simmered for 3–4 hours to make a rich broth, then the meat is removed from the bones for soups, stews or roasts. Cheeks are often pan‑fried or braised with vegetables. The brain can be quickly sautéed or made into a pâté. Tongue is usually boiled, peeled and sliced thin for salads or hot dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh head in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before cooking, rinse well and trim excess fat and blood.
